reader.requirement: At --std 85 the Nucleus EXIT statement is the single word EXIT (no operand, no phrase), which the compiler must accept and treat as a no-op procedure end point; every later-edition form (EXIT PERFORM [CYCLE], EXIT PARAGRAPH, EXIT SECTION, EXIT METHOD, EXIT FUNCTION, EXIT PROGRAM RAISING) must be refused at 85, while EXIT PROGRAM (the 1985 Inter-Program Communication module's own format) stays legal.

edition-consulted.switches: Check(ExitPerform2002 / ExitParagraph2002 / ExitSection2002 / ExitMethodWindow / ExitFunctionWindow) refuse the later forms below 2002; ExitProgramArchaic2023 and ExitProgramNotLast2002 for EXIT PROGRAM; the bare EXIT arm calls no Check at any edition
the RAISING tail of EXIT PROGRAM is refused COBOL0879 below 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 2002 and later EXIT gains PERFORM [CYCLE], PARAGRAPH, SECTION, METHOD, FUNCTION and RAISING forms, all refused COBOL0900/0879 at 85; bare EXIT binds to BoundNop at every edition

reader.notes: The grammar is a superset (exitStatement admits every later form); the 1985 format is enforced by VersionConformancePass gates for each later form, all probed and refused at 85, and bare EXIT binds to BoundNop. The format's one word is too short for a cite.py quotation, so the function, SR1 and GR1 are cited. Diagnostics cite §2023 text at --std 85.
